text.p: ZAGREB, Aug 14 - Following are highlights of the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Tourism Ministry says the current tourist season may rake in an excess of $2.5 billion.
- Trade unions claim some 100,000 workers are not receiving their monthly wages and these figures are rising.
- Italy, Germany and Bosnia and Herzegovina top the list of Croatia's export partners. Croatia's six-month export totals $4.2 billion up from $3.5 billion in the same period of 1996.
- Croatia team football players lose to the Newcastle squad by 2-1.
- The Central Bank's foreign reserves have grown to $2.4 billion and are up since the start of the year by $67 million.
- Audi-Volkswagen may enter Croatia through a possible deal whereby the A-3 car would be put together in Sibenik's TLM metalworks.

- Prices of assorted PIK Vrbovec meat products may drop by six to seven percent, while the prices of some types of fresh meat produced by the same company should drop by up to 40 percent, in line with last week's announcement by the Agriculture and Forestry Minister Zlatko Dominikovic.
- The blood banks in Zagreb hospitals are so drained that there is only enough blood supplies to cover the need of emergency surgery.
- Some 27 Croatian Serbs who have been living in Eastern Slavonia are heading back to their homes in Zadar and Korenica.
- Mladen Naletilic Tuta should either have charges filed against him or be freed from custody by August 26.
- Out of 882 outdoor fires burning in the first six months of this year and destroying 2,082 hectares of woodland in Croatia's coastal areas, 133 were set alight on purpose.
- Some 7,000 mostly foreign guests are staying on the island of Hvar. -- Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075
